cohort: Ten women with at least one live birth pregnancy after kidney transplantation followed at a tertiary hospital between 2000 and 2021
finding: Pregnancies after kidney transplantation were associated with a range of risks for both the mother (e.g., cesarean sections, emergency deliveries, UTIs, and preeclampsia) and child (e.g., prematurity, lower birth measurements, and a tendency to remain under the 50th percentile in growth charts), while the short- and long-term impact on the allograft appeared reassuring despite a trend toward lower eGFR after pregnancy.
